title: Claude Hopkins compared with Andy Razaf
summary: Hopkins was sedate and well trained with a big band at the Cotton Club, while Razaf was loaded with talent; Johnson collaborated with both.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Isn't that wonderful. You know, another person that I've been looking through, you know, that came to mind is Claude Hopkins. Again, his name is also hardly ever mentioned. And I suppose it's the same thing. You've got some people who've just got more of a promotion orientation or context. Is that it, you think?
Oh, an awful nice kind of guy. A real fine guy. They don't make them any nicer than him.
Of all the people that you collaborated with -- and again we're excluding Fats, because he is in a class by --
With Claude and Andy Razaf and the others. But of all the people --
Now, just can you -- can you kind of describe the difference between working with Claude, say, and working with Andy?

Oh, gosh, it's like night and day. Claude is more sedate and light, and yet and still he's down there -- with Andy, it looks like Andy had more talent than he knew what to do with. He was just loaded with talent. There were so many different things he was... (inaudible), he was terrific, Razaf was. (Inaudible). He was something. Claude was just as qualified as he could possibly be. He knew his music and studied it and he -- several times he had a lot of (inaudible) because he had a big band at one time. He had to take his band (inaudible) at the Cotton Club.

Yeah, he (inaudible) at the Cotton Club. Of course, I remember many times when the Broadway Music Company published songs (inaudible) there was a sheet that they made that you get a certain amount of songs from in a (inaudible) work, where you made that sheet, which meant an awful lot to those publishers.
Well, I could go up and get Claude to do my song anytime. I could go, just take a song out and put my solo in. We were that close.
